spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers; u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth and q∈R^m unit. Assume |u|=1, u_tt−Δ_xu=a u pointwise for some real a, and for every compact time interval J, u=q outside a compact C_J uniformly on J. Define e=|u_t|²+Σ|∂_xj u|² and E=∫R^n e dx. Prove e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E differentiable, and E'(r)=0 for each r>0; no endpoint assertion at 0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

propositions.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r0>0 and choose compact interval J with r0 interior and J⊂(0,∞). H003 supplies C_J. Smoothness and constancy off C_J show u_t and spatial derivatives vanish outside C_J; continuity gives boundary vanishing. Thus e(·,r0) is continuous and compactly supported. Apply M001 to prove integrability.

Take closed box B containing C_J. e_t is continuous on compact B×J. M004 gives uniform continuity there. For each x, M002 applied to t↦e(x,t) expresses its difference quotient as interval average of e_t; derivative and interval integrability follow from smoothness. Uniform continuity gives uniform convergence to e_t(x,r0). B has finite measure, so the integrals converge. E(t)=∫_B e, hence E differentiable at r0 with derivative ∫_B e_t.

Differentiate e: e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j u_j·∂_j u_t. For each j, g_j=u_t·u_j is smooth compactly supported, with ∂_j g_j=(∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj. The derivative is integrable by M001. Coordinate identification R^n=R^(n−1)×R preserves Lebesgue integrability; M003 gives Fubini. For each remaining coordinate, M002 on [−L,L] containing support yields integral ∂_j g_j=0 by zero endpoints. Hence ∫(∂_j u_t)·u_j=−∫u_t·u_jj. Summing yields E'(r0)=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu). Differentiating H001 gives u·u_t=0; H002 makes acceleration a scalar multiple of u, so integrand zero and E'(r0)=0.
As r0>0 was arbitrary, the assertions hold for every positive time; no assertion is made at zero.
